memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: 'Now this is the law of the Nazirite when the period of their dedication is over. They are to be brought to the entrance to the tent of meeting. There they are to present their offerings to the Lord: a year-old male lamb without defect for a burnt offering, a year-old ewe lamb without defect for a sin offering, a ram without defect for a fellowship offering.' - Num 6:13-14 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
When the Nazirite completed their vow, they came to God with offerings — a burnt offering, a sin offering, and a fellowship offering. Even at the joyful end of a season of devotion, the person did not come empty-handed or presuming on their own goodness. They came through sacrifice.

This is important. The Nazirite had spent a whole period set apart for God, giving up wine and comforts, living in special dedication. Anyone might have thought, "Surely now I have earned God's favour." Yet even they still needed a sin offering. Their devotion, however sincere, did not make them sinless.

This guards us against a subtle trap: thinking that our spiritual efforts earn our standing with God. Even our best devotion is imperfect and needs cleansing. We never outgrow our need for atonement.

But notice the fellowship offering too. This was an offering of joy and communion, shared in God's presence. The end of the vow was not only about atonement but about celebration and closeness with God. Devotion led to deeper fellowship.

The good news is that all these offerings find their fulfilment in Jesus. He is our burnt offering, our sin offering, and the One through whom we have fellowship with God. Because of Him, we can draw near — not trusting our own devotion, but resting in His finished work, and enjoying real communion with our God.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you ever think your spiritual efforts earn God's favour?
- How does it humble you that even our best devotion needs cleansing?
- How does Christ give you both atonement and fellowship with God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, keep me from trusting my own devotion. Thank You that through Christ I am cleansed and welcomed into real fellowship with You. Amen.
